content.rationale: Bottleneck Mahalanobis distance is sensitive to near-OOS held-out intents, while encoder-space distance captures broader domain shifts; train-fitted robust scaling makes their additive fusion comparable.

ViM-style residual norm measures encoder components unsupported by the principal in-scope feature subspace, while energy captures classifier uncertainty. A train-fitted robust scale makes the two signals comparable without using evaluation-set statistics.

A moderately large k-nearest-neighbour radius in L2-normalized bottleneck space measures whether an item lies in a locally supported in-scope semantic region. Using k=32 reduces sensitivity to isolated training examples while retaining sensitivity to sparse near-OOS regions.
